chain.placement: Chipmaking equipment: ion implanters, tools used in making chips. The release concerns this equipment only; it does not concern chips themselves, advanced computing or chip design.

facts.text: Two rules were announced; BIS says they restrict the PRC’s ability to obtain advanced computing chips, develop and maintain supercomputers, and manufacture advanced semiconductors.
It adds certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related items to the CCL, and license requirements for exporting items to develop or produce such equipment.

comparison.text: Both concern semiconductor manufacturing equipment and China. The October 2022 release announced new license requirements, including for certain chipmaking equipment. This release concerns shipments made in 2021 and 2022 without the license required for a company on the Entity List, and it does not cite the October 2022 rules, so by itself it says nothing about how those rules were enforced.
comparison.title: Commerce restricts advanced computing and chipmaking items for the PRC

readout.text: A settlement agreement between BIS and Applied Materials Inc. and Applied Materials Korea, Ltd., with a penalty of approximately $252 million: twice the transaction value and, BIS says, the maximum allowed by statute.
The requirement the release says was violated: BIS's requirement to obtain a license before shipping to a company on the Entity List.
Any reference to the October 2022 rules on advanced computing and semiconductor manufacturing items.
The equipment: ion implanters, which the release calls semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
Shipments in 2021 and 2022, worth approximately $126 million, first to the Korean affiliate for assembly and then onward to China, without an export license.
The customer's name, what it produced, and how many tools were shipped.
Announced on February 12, 2026. The customer was placed on the Entity List in 2020; the shipments were made in 2021 and 2022.
When the shipments came to BIS's attention, and the dates of the order and the settlement agreement.
Multiple audits of the export compliance program, with annual certifications to BIS in connection with those audits.
Any further terms: the release refers readers to the full order and settlement agreement, available online.
Whether the company disclosed the shipments itself.
